study type: Retrospective observational study with an intervention arm
exposure: knowing their midwife in advance (known midwife project)
prevalence of health problems before second pregnancy
fear of childbirth before second pregnancy
outcome: change in birth preference (from CS to vaginal)
mode of birth (vaginal vs. CS) for second pregnancy
rate of complications in first birth
prevalence of health problems and labour complications in second pregnancy
cohort: The study included 129 second-time mothers who initially expressed a desire for a caesarean section.
finding: The 'known midwife project' helped 81% of participating women (48 out of 129) who initially wanted a caesarean section to give birth vaginally.
mod_finding: Among the women who participated in the 'known midwife group', 81% gave birth vaginally, demonstrating a significant reduction in caesarean section on demand for this sub-group.
